question: Which medication is given as an antidote for organophosphate poisoning to dry up secretions?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Adrenaline
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Diazepam

question: How do cooperative savings schemes help improve maternal health outcomes?

options.A: They remove the need for antenatal checkups at primary health centers
options.B: They reduce transport delays caused by a lack of funds during obstetric emergencies
options.C: They eliminate all medical complications associated with multiple births
options.D: They provide free medical degrees to pregnant women in rural areas

explanation: Having money saved up helps families pay for transport and treatment quickly during an emergency. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which factor plays a major role in causing the ductus arteriosus to constrict after birth?

question: A student comes to the school clinic with a severe, worsening asthma attack that does not respond to initial campus treatment. What is the appropriate role for the nurse to take next?

options.A: Instruct the student to teach other classmates about managing asthma.
options.B: Act as a referral agent and send the student to a hospital immediately.
options.C: Wait until the end of the school day to see if the breathing improves.
options.D: Inspect the school kitchen for any food allergens that caused the attack.

explanation: When a condition exceeds the scope of school care, transferring the student to a higher health facility is necessary. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T5#BMP126_U3_T5_h2)

question: A midwife notices a postpartum patient is bleeding heavily and immediately checks vital signs and fundal tone. Which step of the framework does checking vital signs represent?

options.A: Gather data
options.B: Generate solutions
options.C: Evaluate outcomes
options.D: Identify the problem

explanation: Assessing vital signs and fundal tone is part of collecting objective information to understand the extent of the clinical issue. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the main goal of performing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

options.A: To find the exact staff member to fire after a bad clinical outcome
options.B: To uncover underlying systemic failures that allowed an adverse event to happen
options.C: To satisfy insurance companies so they can pay out financial claims
options.D: To prove that the hospital administration bears no responsibility for errors

explanation: RCA investigates the deep institutional and process causes of errors rather than stopping at human blame. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T4#BMP312_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is it usually ineffective for a midwife to tell an adult client to completely stop eating their traditional cultural foods?

options.A: It ignores economic realities and cultural habits, making the advice unsustainable
options.B: Traditional foods contain zero nutritional value under any circumstance
options.C: Cultural dishes are chemically engineered to resist digestion
options.D: Clients will instantly lose all their body weight within twenty-four hours

explanation: Successful counseling adapts local foods through better preparation methods rather than banning familiar and cherished meals. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T6#BMP118_U3_T6_h6)

question: What happens when the sympathetic nervous system triggers venoconstriction during sudden blood loss?

options.A: Stored blood is squeezed out of veins to maintain blood pressure
options.B: Blood flow to the heart stops entirely until bleeding slows down
options.C: Venous valves open up to let extra fluid leak into body tissues
options.D: Veins relax completely to allow more blood to pool in the legs

explanation: Constricting the veins reduces their storage capacity, pushing reserved blood back into circulation to support vital organs during hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T16#BMP111_U5_T16_h4)

question: Which type of validity involves experts reviewing a tool to check if it covers all parts of a topic?

options.A: Content validity
options.B: Predictive validity
options.C: Concurrent validity
options.D: Face validity

explanation: Content validity relies on experts checking whether the tool comprehensively covers every necessary dimension of the studied topic. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h4)

question: What temporary model is used to form most long bones in the embryo before ossification?

options.A: Dense connective tissue
options.B: Calcified tendon
options.C: Hyaline cartilage
options.D: Fibrous membrane

explanation: Long bones develop from a hyaline cartilage model that is gradually replaced by bone tissue. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T3#BMP111_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the most important rule to follow when changing a wound dressing to keep new bacteria out?

options.A: Using clean unsterile household gloves for speed
options.B: Strict adherence to aseptic technique and hand hygiene
options.C: Warming the dressing materials before application
options.D: Applying heavy amounts of perfumed antiseptic lotion

explanation: Good hand washing and sterile techniques stop outside germs from getting into the open wound. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary function of red bone marrow?

options.A: Blood cell production
options.B: Energy fat storage
options.C: Cartilage lubrication
options.D: Nerve impulse relay

explanation: Red bone marrow is responsible for hematopoiesis, creating red cells, white cells, and platelets. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T3#BMP111_U2_T3_h5)

question: How do people usually catch soil-transmitted worm infections?

options.A: Through mosquito bites during the rainy season
options.B: By walking barefoot on contaminated soil
options.C: By breathing in dust from dry farmland
options.D: Through direct skin contact with infected persons

explanation: Worm larvae in contaminated soil can actively penetrate human skin when individuals walk barefoot. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T10#BMP124_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is the main feature of the classic lecture teaching method?

options.A: It focuses solely on practical bedside patient care
options.B: It requires students to work in small clinical groups
options.C: It relies entirely on independent student computer research
options.D: It is a teacher-centred oral presentation of information

explanation: A lecture is basically an oral presentation delivered by the instructor to a group of learners. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h1)

question: What should you avoid writing when recording observations found during hygiene care?

options.A: Writing vague, unmeasurable opinions like 'patient is fine'
options.B: Documenting the procedure time and date accurately
options.C: Reporting unusual rashes to the senior midwife
options.D: Noting exact measurements of any skin redness

explanation: Vague statements lack clinical usefulness and do not provide clear information for other healthcare team members. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T1#BMP110_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the fluid-filled cavity inside a developing blastocyst called?

options.A: Amniotic sac
options.B: Chorionic villus
options.C: Blastocoele
options.D: Yolk sac

explanation: The fluid-filled space that forms inside the blastocyst is the blastocoele or blastocystic cavity. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T3#BMP210_U4_T3_h4)

question: A midwife gives an asthma medication via inhaler to a pregnant woman. What is the most important clinical action to perform shortly after the procedure?

options.A: Assess the patient's breathing sounds and respiratory rate
options.B: Keep the patient lying completely flat on her back for an hour
options.C: Record the batch number of the inhaler in the main ledger
options.D: Restrict all oral fluids for the next four hours

explanation: Evaluating clinical parameters helps the midwife determine if the medication successfully opened the airways and eased breathing. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T5#BMP120_U2_T5_h6)

question: According to modern definitions by bodies like the International Council of Nurses, who receives nursing care?

options.A: Individuals admitted only for infectious diseases
options.B: Both sick and well people in all settings
options.C: Only critically ill patients in tertiary hospitals
options.D: Patients recovering exclusively from major surgeries

explanation: Nursing goes beyond treating disease to include health promotion and wellness for healthy individuals across various environments. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a major mechanical function of the dermal papillae?

options.A: Locking the epidermis and dermis tightly together
options.B: Storing large reserves of Vitamin D
options.C: Producing high amounts of subcutaneous fat
options.D: Secreting thick oily sebum onto the skin surface

explanation: The undulating, finger-like design of dermal papillae creates a strong bond that prevents the skin layers from sliding apart easily. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T2#BMP111_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of fine body hairs detecting very light air movement?

options.A: To help sweat evaporate faster during high physical exertion
options.B: To stimulate the sebaceous glands to produce more oil
options.C: To warn the nervous system of insects or touching objects
options.D: To keep the underlying fat layer warm in cold environments

explanation: Nerve endings wrapped around hair follicles detect subtle movements like a crawling insect, serving an early warning sensory function. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T8#BMP111_U4_T8_h3)

question: Who primarily introduced Western-style formal nursing training to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: International trade merchants and explorers
options.B: Christian missionaries and colonial administrators
options.C: United Nations peacekeeping forces
options.D: Local traditional birth attendants and herbalists

explanation: Missionaries and the colonial government established the earliest Western hospitals and nursing schools in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a way that clinical disinfectants destroy bacteria?

options.A: Damaging essential cell proteins
options.B: Strengthening the peptidoglycan cell wall
options.C: Disrupting the outer cell membrane
options.D: Stopping critical metabolic pathways

explanation: Disinfectants work by breaking down or damaging bacterial structures—they never make the cell wall stronger. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T1#BMP116_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why do midwives and public health workers view schools as an important part of community healthcare?

options.A: Schools concentrate large populations of growing children where health interventions easily reach them.
options.B: Children spend more time in boarding schools than with their biological families.
options.C: Midwives are legally required to teach classes in primary schools daily.
options.D: School classrooms have better medical equipment than standard primary health clinics.

explanation: Gathering children in one place makes schools efficient hubs for mass health programs like immunizations and nutrition checks. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T4#BMP126_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering vasopressors like norepinephrine during shock?

options.A: To constrict blood vessels and raise blood pressure
options.B: To lower the patient's heart rate to a normal rhythm
options.C: To thin the blood and prevent dangerous clots
options.D: To put the patient into a deep sleep for surgery

explanation: Vasopressors tighten widened blood vessels, which helps push blood pressure back up to safe levels. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T5#BMP120_U4_T5_h6)

question: During a vaginal exam, a midwife notices the baby's head is not flexing or turning as expected. Why is writing this down immediately so important?

options.A: To detect abnormal progress and intervene before complications arise.
options.B: To prevent the need for any further vaginal examinations.
options.C: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby before delivery.
options.D: To prove that the mother is not pushing hard enough during contractions.

explanation: Catching labor delays or unusual positioning early helps the midwife take action before the mother or baby faces serious distress. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T4#BMP212_U2_T4_h8)

question: Approximately what percentage of blood plasma is made up of water?

options.A: 92 percent
options.B: 55 percent
options.C: 7 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Water forms the vast majority of plasma at roughly 92 percent, providing the fluid medium for transport. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T1#BMP111_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical tool used by midwives during labor to prevent prolonged labor from progressing to obstruction?

options.A: The partograph
options.B: The ultrasound scanner
options.C: The fetal scalp electrode
options.D: The pelvimeter

explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of labor progress, alerting the midwife when cervical dilation crosses the alert or action lines. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T3#BMP311_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a major problem for the baby that is directly linked to placental malaria?

options.A: Permanent neonatal blindness
options.B: Macrosomia and high birth weight
options.C: Low birth weight and fetal growth restriction
options.D: Congenital bone malformations

question: What is the main goal of first aid in an emergency?

options.A: To provide definitive surgical treatment at the scene
options.B: To document legal details before touching the patient
options.C: To preserve life and prevent the condition from worsening
options.D: To completely cure the patient of the underlying disease

question: Why is a good patient assessment so important before you start the implementation phase?

options.A: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.B: It completely eliminates the need to document care later
options.C: It replaces the requirement for writing a formal care plan
options.D: It ensures the chosen interventions match current patient needs

explanation: Solid baseline data helps ensure the care you provide is safe and relevant to the patient's actual condition. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T5#BMP120_U1_T5_h1)

question: How does the inner spongy arrangement help an irregular bone function?

options.A: It absorbs shock and keeps the skeleton lightweight.
options.B: It prevents blood vessels from entering the bone marrow.
options.C: It completely stops any risk of bone fractures.
options.D: It allows the bone to stretch significantly during movement.

explanation: The structure of spongy bone distributes weight and cushions impact while keeping the bone relatively light. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T6#BMP111_U2_T6_h2)

question: A pregnant woman feels a gentle touch on her forearm. Which dermal structure initially helps her detect this light sensation?

options.A: Arrector pili muscles
options.B: Meissner corpuscles
options.C: Pacinian corpuscles
options.D: Sweat gland ducts

question: Which physical sign describes a 'board-like abdomen' in peritonitis?

options.A: Abdominal muscle rigidity
options.B: Visible peristaltic waves
options.C: Hyperactive bowel sounds
options.D: Shifting dullness on percussion

question: What is a main reason for giving intravenous atropine in an emergency?

options.A: Extreme hypertension
options.B: Acute postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Severe bradycardia
options.D: Sudden anaphylactic shock

explanation: Atropine blocks vagal input to the heart, safely increasing a dangerously low heart rate during emergencies. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T5#BMP124_U2_T5_h4)

question: What primary force pushes fluid across the glomerular membrane during filtration?

options.A: Active cellular transport
options.B: Capillary hydrostatic pressure
options.C: Smooth muscle peristalsis
options.D: Osmotic pull from large proteins

explanation: Blood pressure inside the glomerular capillaries pushes water and small solutes through the filtration membrane. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T3#BMP121_U3_T3_h2)

question: What happens inside a cell when it runs out of energy during prolonged shock?

options.A: The cell starts producing extra oxygen to save the surrounding tissue
options.B: Sodium and water flood inside, causing the cell to swell and burst
options.C: Cellular walls become completely impenetrable to all fluids
options.D: The cell creates a protective shell and goes into a deep sleep

question: Within how many hours after delivery should anti-D immunisation be given to an Rh-negative mother to work best?

options.A: 2 weeks
options.B: 1 week
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 72 hours

question: What type of consent generally applies when an unconscious patient needs emergency life-saving care?

options.A: Delayed court consent
options.B: Implied consent
options.C: Family committee consent
options.D: Written informed consent

explanation: When a person is unconscious and facing a life-threatening situation, the law assumes they would want emergency treatment. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T1#BMP110_U7_T1_h6)

question: A patient preparing a home nasal saline rinse asks what kind of water is safest to use. What should the midwife advise?

options.A: Straight from the tap
options.B: Sparkling soda water
options.C: Boiled and cooled water
options.D: Ice cold mineral water

question: Why is heavy medical jargon discouraged when explaining care plans to pregnant mothers?

options.A: It can confuse patients and lead to misunderstandings about their treatment.
options.B: It is forbidden by international copyright laws in healthcare.
options.C: Midwives are legally barred from knowing any scientific terminology.
options.D: Patients prefer reading heavy textbooks instead of talking.

explanation: Clear, plain language ensures the patient truly comprehends her health status and what is expected of her care plan. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h6)

question: What happens when one medicine changes how the body handles a second medicine taken at the same time?

options.A: A genetic polymorphism
options.B: Enzyme saturation
options.C: A drug-drug interaction
options.D: Physiological tolerance

explanation: A drug-drug interaction occurs when two or more substances mix in the body and alter each other's effects or safety. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T6#BMP124_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is a major risk when medical equipment is poorly maintained?

options.C: It shortens machinery lifespan and risks inaccurate clinical readings
options.D: It automatically increases the patient admission rate in the ward

explanation: Neglected equipment breaks down faster and can give faulty measurements, leading to poor clinical decisions. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is an essential daily foot care practice for someone living with diabetes?

options.A: Walking barefoot indoors to toughen the skin

options.C: Checking the feet daily for cuts, sores, or redness

question: Where in the body is simple squamous epithelium found to help with rapid diffusion?

options.A: Surface of the sweat glands
options.B: Outer layer of the skin
options.C: Lining of the urinary bladder
options.D: Air sacs of the lungs

explanation: The ultra-thin nature of simple squamous epithelium in the lung air sacs allows for the fast exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T6#BMP111_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering general anesthesia during difficult cases of uterine inversion?

options.C: To stop all active postpartum hemorrhaging instantly
options.D: To relax the uterine myometrium for replacement

question: Which laboratory result helps clinicians tell HHS apart from diabetic ketoacidosis?

options.A: Absence of any blood urea nitrogen
options.B: Extremely low serum potassium levels
options.C: Normal or near-normal arterial blood pH
options.D: Completely clear and normal urine output

question: How are synovial joints classified based on how much they can move?

question: Why is having the placenta divided into multiple separate cotyledons beneficial for the fetus?

options.A: It helps the uterus contract more forcefully during the third stage of labor

options.C: It allows the fetus to practice breathing movements inside the amniotic sac

question: What should a midwife look for when inspecting a patient's hair during a routine physical assessment?

options.A: Skin turgor on the forearm
options.B: Color, texture, and distribution
options.C: Internal core body temperature
options.D: Blood pressure and pulse rate

question: A new mother with schizophrenia reports hearing a voice telling her to drop her baby. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Document the statement in the case notes and check back the next day
options.B: Discharge the mother home immediately so she can rest in a quiet bedroom
options.C: Advise the mother to ignore the voice and try sleeping for a few hours
options.D: Ensure the immediate physical safety of the baby and secure constant supervision

question: Why is blood group O considered the universal red cell donor?

options.C: The red blood cells lack both A and B antigens
options.D: The blood cells multiply faster than other types

question: What is the main difference between a cream and an ointment?

options.A: Creams are water-and-oil emulsions that wash off easily, whereas ointments are greasy and oil-based.

options.C: Creams contain alcohol to dry out weeping wounds while ointments add moisture.
options.D: Creams are solid blocks meant to melt at body temperature inside body cavities.

explanation: Creams mix water and oil together, meaning they wash off easily and do not leave a heavy, greasy feel like pure ointments do. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T4#BMP120_U2_T4_h3)

question: What dangerous event occurs when bowel pressure cuts off the blood supply completely?

options.C: Rapid lengthening of the small intestine

question: Where are eccrine sweat glands mostly found on the body?

options.C: Only on the palms and soles of the feet

question: What is evidence-based practice in nursing primarily built upon?

options.C: Personal opinions of senior medical consultants
options.D: Strict hospital traditions and ancient folklore

question: What is the single most effective lifestyle measure a patient can take to prevent recurrent kidney stones?

options.A: Taking daily high-dose Vitamin C supplements
options.B: Avoiding all physical exercise to prevent mineral shaking
options.C: Drinking enough fluids to maintain a high daily urine output

question: What is the primary role of the manager during the directing phase?

question: A patient just finished receiving her intravenous loading dose of magnesium sulfate. What step comes next?

question: What are the three core mandates of tertiary health institutions in Nigeria?

question: Which of these is NOT a reason to urgently refer someone for psychiatric help after an emergency?

question: Which substance in sweat actively helps destroy bacteria on the skin?

question: A bleeding postpartum mother is stabilized at a clinic. What must happen before she is placed in the ambulance?

question: What happens to cranial sutures as a person transitions from infancy to adulthood?

explanation: Substances like oxygen move naturally from an area of higher concentration in the blood to an area of lower concentration in the tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h3)

question: Which factor strengthens and stabilizes a loose fibrin mesh into a tough clot?

options.A: Factor III
options.B: Factor XIII
options.C: Factor X
options.D: Factor V

explanation: Factor XIII, also known as fibrin-stabilizing factor, links fibrin strands together to give the blood clot strength. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T9#BMP111_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of emotional or spiritual distress in a terminally ill patient?

options.A: Interest in hospital paperwork
options.B: A sudden increase in daily appetite
options.C: Deep restlessness and open expressions of fear
options.D: A stable heart rate and normal blood pressure

explanation: Unresolved emotional or spiritual burdens often manifest outwardly as restlessness, anxiety, and verbalized fears. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T4#BMP120_U5_T4_h3)

question: What term describes moving a limb toward the midline of the body?

options.A: Abduction
options.B: Extension
options.C: Pronation
options.D: Adduction

explanation: Adduction brings a body part toward the central axis of the body, whereas abduction moves it away. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why do many women experience noticeable hair shedding a few months after giving birth?

options.A: The physical stress of labor immediately destroys all active hair follicles in the scalp

options.C: Excessive washing of the newborn baby transfers hair loss hormones to the mother
options.D: High pregnancy hormones keep hair in the resting phase, which then shed together postpartum

explanation: High estrogen levels during pregnancy prolong the growth phase, causing many hairs to enter the resting phase simultaneously and shed after delivery. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T8#BMP111_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary reason a person with bronchitis develops a persistent cough?

options.A: Severe spasm of the outer chest wall muscles
options.B: Sudden collapse of the tiny air sacs in the lungs
options.C: Complete blockage of the upper nasal passages
options.D: Swelling and extra mucus production in the airways

explanation: Irritation of the bronchial tubes causes swelling and excess mucus, which the body tries to clear through coughing. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T5#BMP125_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard newborn genital check for a male infant?

options.A: Measuring the exact length of the vas deferens

options.C: Checking the position of the urethral meatus
options.D: Inspecting the penis for abnormal curvature or swelling

question: Which health model defines wellness strictly as the absence of physical signs of disease?

options.A: Eudaimonistic model
options.B: Clinical model
options.C: Role performance model
options.D: Adaptive model

explanation: The clinical model focuses narrowly on the medical signs of sickness and considers a person healthy if no disease is found. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T3#BMP110_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary biological purpose of excretion in the human body?

options.A: Digesting complex food proteins
options.B: Removing toxic metabolic waste products
options.C: Producing new red blood cells
options.D: Storing excess dietary vitamins

explanation: Excretion clears out unwanted waste materials so they do not build up and harm body tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T7#BMP111_U4_T7_h1)

question: A patient who had surgery ten days ago suddenly starts bleeding from the wound because of an infection. How is this bleeding classified?

options.A: Primary haemorrhage
options.B: Secondary haemorrhage
options.C: Accidental haemorrhage
options.D: Reactionary haemorrhage

explanation: Bleeding occurring a week or more after surgery, linked to infection or tissue breakdown, is classified as secondary haemorrhage. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T4#BMP120_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why does an Rh-negative person usually not have anti-Rh antibodies in their blood at birth?

options.A: The body destroys these specific antibodies during fetal life
options.B: Rh antigens are identical in both positive and negative humans
options.C: Antibodies only form after exposure to Rh-positive cells
options.D: Placental barriers completely block the production of all globulins

explanation: Unlike the ABO system, Rh antibodies are immune antibodies that require a previous exposure to develop. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T7#BMP111_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which precursor molecule do the Leydig cells primarily use to synthesize testosterone?

options.A: Cholesterol
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cholesterol serves as the foundational raw material for creating steroid hormones, including testosterone. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T5#BMP210_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which organ mainly produces thrombopoietin, the hormone that stimulates platelet production?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Pancreas
options.C: Liver
options.D: Adrenal gland

explanation: The liver produces most of the body's thrombopoietin, which tells the bone marrow to make more platelets. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T4#BMP111_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which sign best indicates that a grieving mother has reached acceptance?

options.A: She insists her baby is hidden in the ward
options.B: She speaks about her loss with calm sorrow and plans for the future
options.C: She directs insults at the nursing staff
options.D: She refuses to speak and cries at every sound

explanation: Reaching acceptance allows individuals to process sorrow constructively and look ahead. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is cigarette smoking discouraged for people with gastritis?

options.A: Nicotine increases gastric acid and delays mucosal healing
options.B: Smoking causes immediate complete paralysis of the stomach
options.C: Smoking stops the liver from producing digestive enzymes
options.D: Nicotine turns the stomach lining black permanently

explanation: Smoking stimulates acid production and constricts blood vessels in the stomach, which slows down the healing process. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T4#BMP125_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is pointing and calling a specific staff member's name important when delegating during an emergency?

options.A: It speeds up the process of writing the patient case notes
options.B: It ensures senior staff members always get the easiest tasks
options.C: It prevents diffusion of responsibility among team members
options.D: It is a strict legal requirement for nursing documentation

explanation: When a leader singles someone out by name, it removes ambiguity so everyone knows exactly who is responsible for the task. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the main risk for healthcare workers who deal with trauma day after day without proper rest?

options.A: Compassion fatigue and burnout
options.B: Complete immunity to all future stress
options.C: Sudden improvement in night vision
options.D: Increased physical height and bone density

explanation: Seeing trauma repeatedly without taking time to rest emotionally can lead to exhaustion and emotional burnout. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T10#BMP110_U7_T10_h7)

question: What main feature sets adaptive immunity apart from innate immunity?

options.A: Immediate rapid response
options.B: Presence of skin barriers
options.C: Lack of chemical signals
options.D: Specific target recognition

explanation: Adaptive immunity tailors its defense to target specific foreign antigens rather than mounting a generalized response. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T6#BMP111_U6_T6_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a lesson plan in midwifery education?

options.A: To replace the official school curriculum entirely
options.B: To record the disciplinary history of student midwives
options.C: To serve as a structured roadmap for a single teaching session
options.D: To track the monthly salary of the teaching staff

explanation: A lesson plan guides the instructor step-by-step through a specific class period to ensure all learning goals are met. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why does an unconscious patient easily get an blocked airway?

options.A: Relaxed muscles cause the tongue to fall backward.
options.B: The windpipe collapses from lack of air pressure.
options.C: The vocal cords snap shut tightly.
options.D: Extra saliva blocks the nose.

explanation: When throat muscles relax, gravity pulls the tongue back and blocks the upper airway. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference in stool consistency between an ileostomy and a colostomy?

options.A: Colostomy output is always liquid
options.B: Colostomy output contains digestive enzymes
options.C: Ileostomy stool is completely formed
options.D: Ileostomy output is more watery

explanation: Because an ileostomy is formed from the small intestine, water has not yet been absorbed by the colon, making the waste very liquid. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T12#BMP125_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of a nursing diagnosis compared to a medical diagnosis?

options.A: The patient's human response to health conditions
options.B: The administrative classification of the hospital admission
options.C: The specific pharmacological treatment prescribed by a doctor
options.D: The underlying disease pathology and cellular changes

explanation: Nursing diagnoses address how a person reacts physically, emotionally, or socially to health challenges, rather than naming the disease itself. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T1#BMP120_U1_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman presents with chronic diarrhea, severe fatigue, and pale bulky stools that float. Which condition should a midwife suspect?

options.A: Urinary tract infection
options.B: Malabsorption syndrome
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: Fatty floating stools and fatigue point toward an inability to absorb nutrients and fats properly. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T3#BMP121_U2_T3_h8)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Background
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Breathing

question: What is a midwife looking for when pulling down a patient's lower eyelid to check the conjunctiva?

options.A: Bleeding caused by gum disease
options.B: Yellow discoloration indicating jaundice
options.C: Swelling caused by high blood pressure
options.D: Pallor indicating possible anemia

explanation: Pale conjunctiva is a classic physical sign of low hemoglobin levels or anemia during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T1#BMP110_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is the main visual difference between a bar chart and a histogram?

options.A: Histograms can only display two categories
options.B: Bar charts are only drawn using red ink
options.C: Histograms have bars that touch without gaps
options.D: Bar charts use circles instead of rectangles

explanation: Because histograms represent continuous data, the bars touch each other to show that the scale runs smoothly without breaks. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T2#BMP225_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is your main responsibility as a midwife when giving any drug to a patient?

options.A: Ensuring total patient safety
options.B: Ordering new stock from the pharmacy
options.C: Finishing the drug round quickly
options.D: Writing the prescription down

explanation: As the midwife administering the medication at that moment, patient safety is your ultimate responsibility. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T1#BMP120_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which physiological measurement is typically included in a standard MEWS assessment?

options.A: Amniotic fluid volume
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Fundal height measurement
options.D: Urine protein level

explanation: Respiratory rate is a vital sign monitored in MEWS because changes in breathing often indicate early systemic shock or distress. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does the spread of bowel inflammation in ulcerative colitis differ from Crohn disease?

options.A: Ulcerative colitis is confined strictly to the small intestine
options.B: Ulcerative colitis skips sections of healthy tissue throughout the bowel
options.C: Ulcerative colitis penetrates deeply through the muscle wall
options.D: Ulcerative colitis features continuous inflammation starting in the rectum

explanation: Ulcerative colitis spreads continuously upward from the rectum without leaving skipped healthy patches, which helps clinicians tell it apart from Crohn disease. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T10#BMP125_U3_T10_h1)

question: A patient is moving their elbow back and forth in a single plane. Which joint shape makes this movement possible?

options.A: Pivot
options.B: Plane
options.C: Hinge
options.D: Saddle

explanation: Hinge joints operate like a door hinge, allowing movement in only one plane, such as bending and straightening the elbow. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h3)

question: What is the main function of the denial stage after a sudden loss?

options.A: Permanently hiding the truth from family
options.B: Acting as a temporary buffer to protect the mind from overwhelming pain
options.C: Speeding up physical recovery
options.D: Punishing the healthcare team

explanation: Denial numbs immediate shock, giving the individual time to slowly process reality at their own pace. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is a primary example of system software?

options.A: A word processing document

options.D: An operating system

explanation: Operating systems like Windows or Linux manage core hardware and provide a platform for other programs, making them system software. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T3#BMP123_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which layer of the gastrointestinal tract wall is primarily responsible for peristalsis and moving food forward?

options.A: Submucosa

question: Why does a pregnant woman often feel short of breath even with a normal respiratory system?

options.A: Lung tissue shrinks significantly in size

question: Why is Nightingale's emphasis on clean surroundings and efficient drainage still critical for maternity care today?

options.A: It ensures that doctors do not have to perform physical examinations

options.C: It helps prevent postpartum and neonatal infections in resource-limited settings
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital will receive international funding grants

explanation: Good sanitation and waste management directly reduce the risk of deadly puerperal sepsis and newborn infections in environments facing infrastructural challenges. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T6#BMP110_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is checking the kidneys especially important during pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy causes major physiological changes that can mask or trigger renal problems

options.C: Routine lab tests are completely ineffective without specialized equipment
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering waste entirely during the second trimester

question: What are the three main parts of the adult human breastbone or sternum?

question: Why is understanding fluid balance especially important when caring for pregnant women?

options.C: Pregnancy causes massive shifts in maternal blood volume and fluid handling
options.D: Pregnant women completely stop losing water through normal respiration

question: Why does severe gum disease with bleeding put a person at risk for endocarditis?

options.C: It lowers their overall blood pressure dangerously
options.D: It introduces oral bacteria directly into the bloodstream

question: What is the name of the basic structural and functional unit of the human kidney?

question: Between which two anatomical landmarks is the tape placed when measuring Mid-Upper Arm Circumference?

question: What term describes white blood cells squeezing through the gaps of blood vessel walls into damaged tissue?

question: How does the innate immune system recognize different invading germs?

options.C: By storing past infection records inside specialized B-lymphocytes
options.D: By waiting for T-cells to identify the specific strain of bacteria

question: Which of the following best describes a syndesmosis joint?

options.C: Completely fused bone plates with zero flexibility
options.D: Bones connected by longer fibers allowing slight movement

question: What is the main purpose of a test blueprint when planning a midwifery exam?

question: What happens when a hormone level gets too high in a standard negative feedback system?

question: Which level sits at the absolute base of Maslow's human needs pyramid?

question: What is a key feature of a primary immune response to a new pathogen?

options.A: It clears the foreign microbe within a few hours

options.C: It prevents all future infections from occurring
options.D: It is slow and usually accompanied by clinical illness

question: What does it mean when we say the researcher is the main instrument in a qualitative study?

question: A woman develops a severe uterine infection after an unsterile abortion, with rapid shock and dark red urine. Which organism is most likely responsible?

options.C: Staphylococcus aureus

question: A woman in active labor has weak contractions, a soft uterus, and no pelvic blockage. What is a common way to help?

question: How does adhesion differ from apposition in early implantation?

question: What is the primary reason for elevating the head of the bed slightly after placing a bedpan?

question: Why do core muscles activate slightly BEFORE you lift a heavy object?

question: Which of these is a key focus during clinical bedside teaching?

question: What is the term for a birth defect where the spinal column fails to close properly during early growth?

question: Postpartum hemorrhage in a maternity ward most commonly leads to which type of shock?

question: What is a practical way a midwife can help with school health outside the clinic?

options.C: Conducting basic nutritional screenings and growth monitoring

question: When should you check a patient's vital signs before starting a blood transfusion?

question: Why is Ziehl-Neelsen sputum microscopy referred to as an acid-fast test?

question: Why is evaluation considered an ongoing activity?

question: Why is it important to repeat hemoglobin screening at later stages of pregnancy?

question: What is the main job of the pneumotaxic center in the pons?

options.C: To allow voluntary breath-holding during swimming
options.D: To detect low levels of oxygen directly in the blood

explanation: The pneumotaxic center limits the length of an inhalation, helping to prevent over-inflation of the lungs and keeping the breathing rhythm smooth. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T5#BMP121_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which category of patients should be discussed first during a shift handover?

options.A: High-risk or unstable patients
options.B: Clients paying private hospital bills
options.C: Patients being discharged tomorrow
options.D: Patients admitted three weeks ago

explanation: Discussing unstable clients first ensures the incoming team is immediately aware of urgent safety needs. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h2)

question: A patient in the ward shows signs of heavy bleeding after surgery and a falling blood pressure. How should you position them initially?

options.A: Flat on the back with legs slightly raised
options.B: Propped up at a 45-degree angle in bed
options.C: Sitting upright in a comfortable chair
options.D: Lying flat on the stomach with head turned

explanation: Elevating the legs uses gravity to help drain blood from the lower limbs back into the main circulation to support blood pressure. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T4#BMP120_U4_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant woman in labour is resting in bed. Which side-lying posture is most appropriate to prevent supine hypotension syndrome?

options.A: Lateral position
options.B: Trendelenburg position
options.C: Prone position
options.D: Supine position

question: Which visual sign in a fresh urine sample should alert a midwife to a possible urinary tract infection?

options.A: Cloudiness with visible floating particles
options.B: A faint, slightly aromatic scent
options.C: A pale yellow and transparent appearance
options.D: A high volume of total output

explanation: Cloudy urine often contains pus, bacteria, and cellular debris which are signs of inflammation or infection in the urinary tract. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T6#BMP110_U6_T6_h5)

question: A rural clinic does not have a reliable refrigerator to store oxytocin. Which medicine is the best alternative to prevent heavy bleeding after birth?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Intravenous syntocinon
options.D: Ergometrine

explanation: Misoprostol stays stable at room temperature, making it very useful in clinics without cold storage facilities. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h2)

question: What primary mineral gives bones their hard, compressive strength?

options.A: Potassium sulfate
options.B: Magnesium nitrate
options.C: Sodium chloride
options.D: Hydroxyapatite

explanation: Hydroxyapatite crystals deposit around collagen fibers to harden the bone matrix, providing compressive strength against heavy loads. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T2#BMP111_U2_T2_h1)

question: What do we call bleeding that happens inside a body cavity after surgery and cannot be seen on the outside?

options.A: External haemorrhage
options.B: Primary haemorrhage
options.C: Internal haemorrhage
options.D: Reactionary haemorrhage

explanation: Internal bleeding occurs inside closed body cavities like the abdomen. Because it is hidden, it cannot be seen with the naked eye until physical signs of blood loss appear. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T4#BMP120_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is a main feature of full-thickness wounds compared to superficial ones?

options.A: They only affect the top layer of skin and heal in a few hours
options.B: They heal entirely through simple surface cell regeneration
options.C: They extend into subcutaneous fat, muscle, or bone and require scarring to heal
options.D: They never require any form of cleaning or dressing

explanation: Full-thickness wounds involve deep tissue loss below the dermis, necessitating granulation and scar tissue formation for repair. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which skin receptor is mainly responsible for detecting fine details, shapes, and textures?

options.A: Merkel discs
options.B: Ruffini endings
options.C: Pacinian corpuscles
options.D: Meissner corpuscles

explanation: Merkel discs are slow-adapting receptors in the lower part of the epidermis that help sense edges, points, and textures clearly. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h3)

question: What role do bile salts play in the digestion and absorption of dietary fats?

options.A: They digest carbohydrates into simple sugars
options.B: They break down large fat drops into tiny droplets
options.C: They actively pump fatty acids across the brush border
options.D: They convert proteins into usable amino acids

explanation: Bile salts break large fat masses into tiny droplets, making it possible for digestive enzymes to work and for fats to be absorbed. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T3#BMP121_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is an open fracture considered a medical emergency requiring immediate attention?

options.A: It always causes permanent paralysis of the limb
options.B: It means the bone has melted inside the muscle
options.C: It carries a very high risk of bone infection
options.D: It heals three times faster than closed breaks

explanation: Exposing broken bone to the outside air allows bacteria to enter the tissue, which can lead to severe bone infection known as osteomyelitis. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T2#BMP216_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why does a midwife need to identify an anthropoid pelvis during pregnancy?

options.A: To know if the mother needs a blood transfusion
options.B: To prevent gestational diabetes
options.C: To figure out the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.D: To understand how the baby will move through the birth canal

explanation: Knowing the pelvic shape helps midwives anticipate how labor will progress and spot any mechanical challenges early. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do many pregnant women experience sluggish digestion and heartburn during gestation?

options.A: The growing fetus completely blocks the production of all digestive enzymes
options.B: Rapid maternal weight gain destroys the villi in the small intestine
options.C: Increased stomach acid production dissolves the esophageal sphincter
options.D: Elevated progesterone levels relax smooth muscle in the digestive tract

explanation: Pregnancy hormones relax smooth muscles throughout the body, slowing down gut motility and leading to common issues like heartburn. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h5)

question: How does the breakdown of an ATP molecule help a transport protein move substances?

options.A: It changes the physical shape of the protein pump
options.B: It cools down the cell to speed up reactions
options.C: It dissolves the surrounding cell membrane entirely
options.D: It attracts water molecules to push the solute forward

explanation: Energy released from ATP alters the shape of the protein, allowing it to move ions across the membrane. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T5#BMP111_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why should an unconscious pregnant woman in shock be placed with a tilt to her left side?

options.A: To keep her from swallowing her saliva
options.B: To stop the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels
options.C: To help lochia drain out of the vagina
options.D: To make it easier to put in an IV line

explanation: Tilting the patient to the left relieves pressure off the aorta and inferior vena cava, keeping blood flowing back to the heart. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of haemostasis in the body?

options.A: To stop bleeding from injured blood vessels
options.B: To regulate overall body temperature
options.C: To transport oxygen to body tissues
options.D: To fight off invading bacterial infections

explanation: Haemostasis is the body's protective process that stops bleeding after a blood vessel gets injured. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T9#BMP111_U5_T9_h1)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is preferred when establishing lines for a patient in severe obstetric shock?

options.A: Small-bore cannulas like 22G or 24G
options.B: Any standard needle size available on the tray
options.C: Large-bore cannulas like 16G or 18G
options.D: Central venous lines inserted exclusively

explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow rapid infusion of intravenous fluids and blood products when every second counts. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T5#BMP311_U4_T5_h4)

question: When a midwife checks a newborn's sucking and rooting reflexes, which group of nerves is mainly being tested?

options.A: Cranial nerves
options.B: Hepatic nerves
options.C: Renal nerves
options.D: Cardiac nerves

explanation: Facial movements, swallowing, and feeding reflexes are controlled by cranial nerves coming from the brainstem. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T1#BMP121_U5_T1_h4)

question: What primary type of tissue holds the bones together in a fibrous joint?

options.A: Loose areolar tissue
options.B: Sponge-like bone marrow
options.C: Hyaline cartilage
options.D: Dense regular connective tissue

explanation: Fibrous joints rely on dense regular connective tissue packed with collagen fibers to bind adjacent bones tightly together without a joint cavity. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T14#BMP111_U2_T14_h1)

question: Where are calcium ions mainly stored inside a resting skeletal muscle fiber?

question: A maternity ward frequently runs out of delivery packs during night shifts due to poor tracking. Which core administrative duty has been neglected?

options.A: Routine antenatal health education delivery
options.B: Immediate postnatal newborn resuscitation
options.C: Direct clinical midwifery assessment of labor
options.D: Material resource management and supply oversight

explanation: Failing to track and stock essential items like delivery packs points directly to a breakdown in resource management rather than clinical assessment skills. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T2#BMP312_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the smooth triangular area on the internal floor of the urinary bladder called?

options.A: Trigone

question: A clinical instructor wants to apply adult learning principles after a student assists in a difficult breech delivery. What should the instructor do?

options.A: Ignore the event because the delivery was already successfully completed
options.B: Ask the student to reflect on what went well and what could be improved
options.C: Give a long lecture on breech mechanics without asking the student any questions
options.D: Tell the student to read the textbook chapter over the weekend as punishment

explanation: Guided reflection encourages self-directed learning and helps adult learners evaluate their own clinical competence. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T1#BMP312_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary role of a reversal agent like flumazenil in an emergency?

options.C: It permanently cures the underlying anxiety disorder

question: Why is it helpful for a midwife to know that the skin is a selective barrier?

options.C: It means medications can never cross the outer layer.

question: A pregnant woman steps up to the scale wearing a heavy wrapper and sandals. What action should the midwife take?

question: Why is it important to follow the ABCDE sequence strictly in emergency care?

options.C: It prevents missing rapidly fatal conditions while distracted by minor injuries
options.D: It ensures that doctors get paid for emergency consultations

question: A pregnant woman has a condition that makes it hard to digest fats. What will happen to her fat-soluble vitamin levels?

options.B: Levels will spike dangerously high due to improper liver storage failure

options.D: Levels will drop because these vitamins rely on dietary fat absorption pathways

question: What should a nurse do when faced with a heavy patient who needs to be moved up in bed?

options.C: Get assistance from another staff member
options.D: Wait until the patient stands up unassisted

question: Why is checking urine or blood ketones an important part of sick-day management education?

options.A: It confirms whether the placenta is functioning normally

question: Which patient requires the highest level of direct nursing observation?

question: How many quadrants is the abdominopelvic cavity divided into for general clinical assessments?

question: A postpartum woman develops a severe uterine infection after a C-section. Which drug combination is a midwife most likely to see prescribed?

question: Where does the primary ossification center typically appear first during endochondral bone formation?

question: Which structure directly secretes synovial fluid into the joint cavity?

question: What clinical action is required when a laboring woman's cervical dilation graph crosses over the action line?

question: How does a well-functioning referral system benefit tertiary teaching hospitals?

question: Why must the neck musculature be specially adapted compared to lower back muscles?

question: Which incoming patient category should receive immediate attention during a busy emergency shift?

question: Which of these does NOT activate pain receptors in the skin?

question: Why might a pregnant woman feel discomfort around her pubic bone late in pregnancy?

question: Which type of virus is usually easier to destroy by simple handwashing with soap or alcohol?

question: What is the main purpose of the appendicular skeleton?

question: What is the main purpose of blood vessels narrowing in the skin during cold exposure?

question: Why does heavy sweating in a hot climate require replacing both water and salts?

question: What is the medical term for the abnormal buildup of fluid in tissue spaces?

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical reason why hospitalized mothers reject standard hospital meals?

question: How many phalanges are found in a normal human foot?

question: Why is it important to record the exact time of death in the nursing notes immediately?

question: Why must a midwife remain at the bedside until the client swallows the medication?

question: What are the firm lumps that often form under the skin over bony pressure points in patients with rheumatoid arthritis called?

question: Which type of peritoneal dialysis uses a mechanical machine called a cycler, usually running overnight?

question: Where does the problem lie in a primary endocrine disorder?

question: Why should a midwife help a bedridden client with daily baths?

question: What is another common name for the bulbourethral glands?

question: A primary three pupil frequently squints when looking at the chalkboard and complains of afternoon headaches. What screening finding is most likely present?

question: Which part of the nail structure contains the living cells responsible for active nail growth?

question: How can facilities best address poor data quality caused by rushed documentation?

question: Why do patients with internal bleeding after surgery sometimes need to return to the operating theatre?

question: Why might a researcher choose NOT to use an RCT for a specific maternal health question?
